### The basketball court is a real earlier setting — and it is in the Central Basin

Week 7 delivered pages 8–10 show Red Leopards playing His Majesty’s Blood at **The Forgotten Court / Central Basin**. These are recovered image bytes, not a reconstruction from a text summary. P08 is “A Game Without Witnesses,” P09 “Every Inch Contested,” and P10 “The Crossover.” The repeated identifying features are the basketball backboard and hoop mounted high on the **right-hand ruined stone wall**, dense ivy, cracked hard court, broken masonry terraces, distant towers and cascades, warm sky and red vegetation. The Belt rests at the court edge; it was not transferred by Red’s basketball win.

The older archived story packet called its Atlas reference `UNRESOLVED-FORGOTTEN-NEUTRAL-COURT`. The delivered artwork supplies a later visible regional caption, **Central Basin**. That resolves what the prior publication told readers, but does not create a registered permanent Atlas location ID. Do not silently relocate the court into Red’s Storm Coast home or claim that the two sports grounds are adjacent.

**Working handling:** `SET-W10-FORGOTTEN-COURT-REVISIT`, region `REG-CENTRAL-BASIN`, existing illustrated venue / Atlas registration pending. This is the old court reused, not a new invented court. Red’s soccer field and the basketball court get a clear geographic cut and an elapsed-time bridge. The existing Rain Escarpment Road and Upper Basin Connector support regional travel; the court’s last local approach is unregistered and remains a modest new connection proposal. No invented distance, travel duration or instantaneous teleportation.

### The soccer field is also recovered, including its current damage

Week 6 PDF pages 6–8 (printed folios 4–6) show the **Theatre of Ruins / Red Leopard Ruins, Storm Coast**: steep stone stands, broken arches, long central field, waterfalls or cliff drops beyond, predator banners and Red–Arsenal football rivalry. The whole illustration, lettering, texture and light form a continuous cinematic page; this is a useful visual-production precedent, not a template to reproduce mechanically.

Week 9 pages 12–14 revisit that soccer territory. P12 shows Red’s raised stone viewing terrace above a rectangular green field with white pitch lines and a white goal; ruined arches and red predator banners ring the space. P13 introduces truck damage. P14 ends with **torn turf, deep ruts, a crushed goal/net and Chins’s truck trapped at the narrow stone arch**. Those conditions cannot disappear merely because Week 10 changes opponents. The truck’s recovery has not been established. Keep the bottleneck outside the principal framing or show only the known damaged approach; do not show the truck restored and conveniently driving elsewhere.

**No nearby river is visibly established in the recovered field pictures.** Jake has now requested one. The proposal is a low-side local river/overflow channel beyond the pitch’s retaining edge, feeding shallow water through the existing drainage opening and truck ruts. This is new local hydrology, explicitly identified as such, consistent with the Storm Coast’s wet exposed escarpment. It is not evidence that the previous art already showed a river.

page_beats.treatment: From a low position just inside the rail, a wide diagonal reveals Chili already running around the ring while DK gains behind him, swinging his own rope overhead. Show all four centaur legs and the single gorilla/equine body clearly. Crowd height and the visible exit gate establish public exposure. Dark Horse is separate, secured at the holding rail outside the active ring if included. The axe is stowed; it does not suddenly cut or block the lasso. Afternoon overcast gives cool fill, sheltered lanterns warm the crowded galleries, and wet hoof tracks define the pursuit line.

Track across the inside of Chili’s attempted turn. DK throws from the established direction, and the catch plus abrupt loss of footing becomes the decisive moment. The rope has a visible continuous route from DK’s hand to Chili, with readable slack/tension; one throw does not magically tie a completed hogtie. Chili’s boot slides through the same churned lane. His decorated hat and sunglasses remain identifiable; the hat may tilt, not disappear. Witness reactions are secondary but legible through the rail. Rain and mud never obscure which character owns the rope.

A low, wider public aftermath shows Chili hogtied in mud at the ring’s center. DK has stopped, braced all four legs and deliberately finished the binding; hand placement and the already caught rope explain the transition. This is humiliating slapstick, not injury spectacle. Chili’s face is readable and clear of the mud. The visible crowd laughs, points and reacts from safe rails. No main cast is teleported in as spectators. A dropped hat at arm’s reach, readable outlaw belt and the expansive empty space between Chili and the gate make the humiliation personal. The shot retains enough of the stands to prove it happened in front of everyone.

page_beats.treatment: Return to the exact Week9 soccer terrace: same arch, field geometry, damaged goal/net and tracks. Red braces a heavy sandbag at a low opening as a shallow river overflow creeps along the torn turf. The first few bags help locally, but water finds the adjacent old rut. Winds pull the predator banners nearly horizontal and shake the goal’s damaged net. A cold pewter sky and dim amber arch lamps replace the earlier bright green confidence. Fallen leaves lodge against the bags; this is November’s exhausted color, not a tropical deluge. The nearby river/overflow connection is a Jake-authorized new geography proposal, not an old image fact. Keep the field flood gentle, with pitch lines still partly visible. No tsunami, building collapse or knee-deep universal flood.

Preserve the right-hand wall-mounted hoop, cracked surface and broken ruin skyline from W7P08–10. Red arrives from the near-left court edge; a snapped branch from the established vegetation margin sweeps toward the right wall. Camera placement echoes the old basketball duel so readers recognize the place before a caption explains it. A distant figure of embodied Niño may occupy the far court in the wind; he remains a humanoid elemental, not a face drawn into a cloud. Wet leaves sweep low along the stone. The strongest gust here can be a local squall funneled by the broken walls even though the basin is farther from the coastal core. Do not introduce a new freestanding basketball pole: the original goal is wall mounted.

The branch has caught the backboard/hoop assembly and bent the rim downward against the same right wall. Red kneels or sits at the near court edge, hands slack and face disbelieving; avoid a second fighting pose. Niño is clearly embodied beyond him, laughing through moving rain and cold light. The ruined support, basketball court lines and old wall remain recognizable. The sports fact behind the taunt is the **2022 Week16 semifinal: Niño 116.32, Red 97.96**, after Red’s 13–1 regular season; Niño subsequently won the championship. A newly written line such as “You remember how that run ended” is fictional dialogue, never an archival quote. A small “2022” reference should be earned by narration or an intentional prop; do not invent an old commemorative plaque.

page_beats.treatment: A wide upward diagonal links the jackhammer’s point at ground level, Chins’s grin, the upper balcony and the family doorway. The first sharply broken concrete reveals deliberate racket, not thunder. TDS emerges above, exactly three heads on one torso: one turns toward the interior, one spots Chins and one begins shouting. The partner’s irritated voice or a soft silhouette behind the door, plus an offscreen baby’s cry, establishes household pressure without inventing an extra lead. Cool southern overcast reflects from waterfall spray; a steady warm interior lamp marks the protected room.

Reverse to a balcony-over-shoulder view: TDS leans forward at the rail, visibly asking for quiet, while below Chins makes eye contact, laughs and reaches to turn up the music before resuming the hammer. The key is acknowledgement followed by indifference. TDS’s heads divide between the crying baby, the furious partner and the offending visitor. One broken paving patch and a short wet dust trail stay in the same positions. Chins is never moved onto the balcony to create a confrontation.

From courtyard level, Chins drives the hammer into a fresh edge of the same expanding patch, grinning toward the balcony while the speaker remains visible. TDS’s whole body is tense; all three heads now direct their frustration outward, yet the family doorway still pulls one eyeline back. This is comic escalation through attention and sound, not physical attack. No thunderclap competes with the deliberate noise at the payoff. The waterfall remains normal background ambience; the baby was settling despite it before Chins began.

**Provisional Game of the Week recommendation: His Majesty’s Blood at D0nkey K0ng**, from the league-audit handoff. Provider home DK is preserved; a neutral fictional preview stage follows the existing GOTW venue convention. History handoff: DK’s franchise alias beat HMB **179.68–111.42 in 2025 Week9**. The league auditor owns that source verification; this visual review uses it as a supplied fact, not a newly inspected historical box score.

**Proposed child set:** `SET-W11-MOUNTAIN-LAKE-BRIDGE-MUSTER` under **`LOC-BRIDGE-MOUNTAIN-LAKE`**, the existing, ownerless **PROVISIONAL_CANON** Bridge at the Mountain Lake, Upper Valleys. Registered landmarks are stone bridge, lake and jump point. This remains a new approach/staging proposal inside the existing location; no new citadel or permanent battlefield is introduced. It serves a wholly different purpose from the rodeo: a narrow public crossing where two powerful arrivals must eventually meet.

**Geographic support:** DK reaches the site by Highland Stronghold Road to Arsenal Barbershop, then Hearthroad to the lake. HMB can approach by Black Cliff Road through the Trade Jedi mountain base and Eastern Ascent. These route links are registered; their exact arrival clock and local side of the bridge are staging proposals. The site is not called DK’s home simply because ESPN lists him home.

**One full-page preview image:** a wide oblique view along the old stone bridge, lake low beneath the arches, two enormous but physically grounded arrivals separated by a visible stretch of empty deck. DK holds the nearer approach, all four legs readable; HMB emerges beyond the opposite stone pier. Their stillness should feel dangerous because each already controls a whole end of the crossing. No opening blow, winner pose, transferred Belt or invented final score. Road-worn steps, repaired parapet stones and weather-pitted old lantern brackets imply long use. Two steady sheltered lamps give the fronts of both figures legibility; cold dusk and advancing cloud fill the lake behind them. A gust pulls both factions’ cloth in the same established direction. Keep the jump point background-small; this is no repeat of a leap or rodeo chase.

**Integrated copy candidate:** “THE CROSSING NARROWS” / “Two heavyweights. One more test before the divisional finish.” The verified 2025 result can appear as a concise historical narration line, explicitly dated, if editorially useful. Current records, injuries and stakes arrive from the source-bound Week11 preview data. The page promises a confrontation; it does not predict one team’s victory. Frame the storm as pressure reaching the upper routes, not an outcome forecast.

### Storm Watch co-headline: El Niño at Slob

Use proposed **`SET-W11-SLOB-TAILGATE-STORM-APPROACH`** under registered **`LOC-SLOB-FOOTHILL-CAMP`** (PROVISIONAL_CANON, Upper Valleys; persistent tailgate yard and rough training ground; Hearthroad access). A smaller landscape beat looks outward from the used tailgate yard across stacked secured kegs toward the exposed road. Slob has shifted the shipment under the old shelter and tightened the canvas; he watches a dark front arrive over the foothill ridges. This continues the beer-delivery material vocabulary without asserting the Week10 truck’s exact destination. An embodied Niño may be a small arriving figure on the road only if the preview needs both principals; the cloud front must never replace his body. Warm yard light, cold ridge cloud, fluttering straps and a functioning drain communicate preparation rather than panic. **Storm growth next week stays conditional on future results**, and the preview supplies no fictional flood or win in advance.
